physics_rationale: Shortened graphite displcer reduced positive reactivity insertion when control rod inserted; graphite tip effect was primary trigger of April 26 excursion (added +2-3 beta on AZ-5 press)

Higher U-235 enrichment reduces sensitivity to void coefficient; more fissile material means moderator not needed as much → positive void coefficient magnitude reduced; additional negative Doppler coefficient at higher temperatures

Added 80 additional fixed absorber rods to reduce steady-state void coefficient; absorbers increase negative reactivity base; reduce void coefficient by inserting neutron poison in core without disturbing control rods

Minimum ORM increased from 15 to 30 rod-equivalents after it was understood that ORM=8 contributed to loss of control. Higher ORM ensures more negative reactivity available for emergency shutdown. ORM=8 at Chernobyl meant insufficient neutron-absorbing rods could be inserted quickly.

Faster rod insertion (12s vs 18-20s) reduces the time window during which graphite tips cause positive reactivity pulse; does not eliminate effect but reduces duration; delayed neutron fraction beta~0.005 means any prompt criticality still milliseconds-fast so faster rods help only at subcritical

Operators prohibited from operating below 700 MWt (about 22% of rated power) in normal operation. Below 700 MWt positive void coefficient dominates over Doppler negative coefficient making reactor unstable. Chernobyl test was at 200 MWt = 6% power = deep in unstable regime. This operational limit was already in place but VIOLATED.

Modified fuel assembly geometry to reduce void coefficient; specific design details classified in USSR/Russia but involved reducing moderator-to-fuel ratio in certain zones to reduce the positive component of void reactivity

Western BWRs also use water as moderator but have NEGATIVE void coefficient; if water boils: fewer thermal neutrons → less fission → power drops (inherently stable). Vs RBMK: graphite moderator remains even if water boils → void coefficient positive at low power. Core design determines stability.
source: IAEA safety guidelines; reactor physics texts

physics_rationale: PWRs: water is both moderator AND coolant; if coolant boiled → complete loss of moderation → reactor shuts down (very strongly negative void coefficient). No graphite moderator means no reactivity source if coolant lost. Fundamental design difference from RBMK.

RBMK had no Western-style reinforced containment building; Soviet design assumed separate confinement of coolant circuits; massive pressure tubes (1661 of them) were individual pressure boundaries; explosion blew off 1000t reactor lid and destroyed all confinement; Western PWR/BWR have 50-100cm thick reinforced containment

17 RBMK reactors operating at time of accident; 6 shut down 1990-2004 (mostly Lithuanian RBMK-1500 Ignalina; Lithuania required to close as EU membership condition); 11 remain in Russia as of 2024 at Leningrad (4x RBMK-1000) and Smolensk (3x) and Kursk (4x)

11 RBMK-1000 reactors still operating in Russia as of 2024; all received post-Chernobyl modifications; extended to 45-60 year design lives; all have higher enrichment (2.8%), shorter graphite tips, higher ORM requirements, faster SCRAM

INSAG-1 (1986) blamed primarily operators for violating procedures. INSAG-7 (1991) revised: BOTH design flaws (positive void coefficient, graphite tip effect, no containment) AND operator violations were necessary causes. Neither alone was sufficient; both together made accident possible.

If reactor is prompt critical (reactivity > beta = 0.65%), it responds on prompt neutron lifetime ~10 microseconds → mechanical control impossible. Chernobyl excursion: reactivity likely +7-10 beta above critical = deep prompt supercriticality. RBMK beta is relatively low because of U-235 fission cross section and neutron spectrum.
source: Nuclear physics; INSAG-7; reactor dynamics textbooks

physics_rationale: At 00:28 on April 26 operators lost power to ~30 MWt (xenon pit); Xenon-135 (t1/2=9.2h) had built up to ~3000 pcm poisoning; operators withdrew many rods to overcome this = set stage for ORM=8. Post-accident: RBMK operators prohibited from attempting xenon burnout by rod withdrawal if in deep xenon pit.
